_readme: Every tunable number the adjudicator uses. Calibration edits this file, never
adjudicate.py: the code computes features, this file decides what they are worth.
Each cell's raw feature vector is written to cells.jsonl alongside its probability,
so a later refit can solve for these weights instead of guessing at them.

clustering._doc: Two source-values are the same value (one copied from the other) when they agree to within relative_tolerance. A cluster votes once, plus copy_vote_increment for each extra member — so three copies of PsychonautWiki cannot outvote one independent measurement.

reliability._doc: Per-source, per-column weights, iterated: uniform start -> outlier rate -> weight -> new consensus -> repeat. rate is smoothed by a Beta prior so a source with four values cannot earn an extreme weight. weight falls linearly from 1.0 at rate 0 to min_weight at rate_cap.

class_prior._doc: Log-normal distribution of the same column across class peers, leave-one-out, as a robust z (0.6745 * (x - median) / MAD). mad_floor_decades stops a tight class from turning a 20% difference into z = 40. A class with fewer than min_members after leave-one-out yields no signal at all, and the cell says so.

slips._doc: A value that is almost exactly 1000x or 10x the consensus is a unit slip (ug read as mg) or a decimal slip, which is a different and much stronger claim than 'somewhat high'.

citation._doc: Fractions of one point of citation quality. A row with a DOI or PMID from a review, graded HIGH, with species and assay recorded, scores 1.0.

features._doc: Logistic weights. Every one multiplies a feature emitted in cells.jsonl. Continuous features are already scaled into roughly [0, 1] by the code (log_delta is decades / 3, class_z is |z| / z_cap).

thresholds._doc: needs_manual fires on any of these. tie_ratio is a two-cluster standoff nothing breaks; class_violation_z judges a value that has no cross-source corroboration at all.

evidence_levels._doc: Independent clusters, not raw values. Below `single` the cell carries no cross-source information and is judged only by its class prior and its own internal consistency.

dosewiki._doc: The dose.wiki join. Numeric columns take at most one record per Piru substance, the best-ranked by relationship then confidence, and only from relationships that name the same molecule. Chemistry takes EVERY mapped record, because two dose.wiki compounds claiming one Piru row IS the finding.
